documents.unit: Rutgers Office of Information Technology (all campuses)
documents.title: Guidance on the use of AI at Rutgers
documents.stance_why: The page sets no single stance: it says guidance "will typically vary depending on the discipline, course, and/or instructor" and that students must follow "their program and instructors' guidance". It adds a default that AI "should not be considered permissible for coursework unless clearly stated", but this is a fallback, with no tiers, so the decision is delegated to instructors.
documents.summary: Universitywide IT guidance (shared by all three campuses) with five short sections: use approved AI tools, academic integrity, confidential data, reviewing AI output, and purchasing. Coursework rules are left to instructors, with a fallback that AI is not permissible unless stated.

units.why: The sentence says the university supplies licensed generative AI tools with safeguards; this is a sanctioned, university-provided tool, so P17 fits better than P50, which is about data protection.
units.anchor: provides access to generative AI tools with protections for use in university work

units.why: "your data will not be used to train the models" describes the privacy benefit of vetted tools, so it is a data-protection and vetted-tool fact (P50).
units.anchor: your data will not be used to train the models underlying the tools

units.why: "only Rutgers-approved AI tools should be used at the university" is a directive to use vetted tools to protect data; P50 (prefer vetted tools) is nearest, though it is stronger than "prefer".
units.anchor: only Rutgers-approved AI tools should be used at the university
units.fit_note: Type says prefer vetted tools; this says only approved tools should be used, a restriction on all university use.

units.why: "will typically vary depending on the discipline, course, and/or instructor" hands academic AI decisions to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: guidance on the appropriate use of AI tools in academic settings will typically vary

units.why: "Faculty should consider providing guidance to students" asks instructors to state AI expectations, but only as a consideration, not a mandatory syllabus statement; nearest is P09.
units.anchor: Faculty should consider providing guidance to students on the use of AI
units.fit_note: Type requires a statement; this only says faculty should consider giving guidance.

units.why: "students are encouraged to review course materials and speak with their instructors" tells unsure students to check expectations with the instructor, so P10.
units.anchor: students are encouraged to review course materials and speak with their instructors

units.why: "should not be considered permissible for coursework unless clearly stated" sets a fallback rule of no AI when instructors are silent, so P06 (fallback), not P01, because it is conditional on instructor communication.
units.anchor: they should not be considered permissible for coursework unless clearly stated or communicated by instructors

units.why: "Students are responsible for understanding and abiding by their program and instructors' guidance" makes students accountable for knowing the rules; no type covers knowing rules exactly, and P29 is about owning submitted work, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding and abiding by their program and instructors
units.frag_end: rules on the use of AI.
units.uncovered_note: Students are responsible for knowing and following their program and instructors' AI rules.

units.why: Quoting Policy 10.2.13, coursework must be "the student's own and created without the aid of impermissible technologies", i.e. submitted work must be the student's own (P29); the integrity-policy tie is secondary.
units.anchor: the student’s own and created without the aid of impermissible technologies, materials, or collaborations

units.why: The page points to the Academic Integrity Policy 10.2.13 as the governing standard and adjudication process for alleged violations, so unauthorized AI use falls under integrity processes (P36).
units.anchor: Details on standards of academic integrity and the process for adjudicating alleged violations
units.fit_note: AI misuse is linked to the integrity policy by reference; the page does not itself say AI misuse is misconduct.

units.why: "Confidential information, Protected Health Information (PHI)... may not be appropriate for use in AI applications" is a data-protection caution (P50), phrased softly.
units.anchor: may not be appropriate for use in AI applications and systems

units.why: The page directs readers to a data classification chart for AI tools and the Information Classification Policy 70.1.2, tying AI use to existing university policy (P77).
units.anchor: this data classification chart for AI tools

units.why: "Always review and verify AI content and outputs" tells users to check AI output, matching P31.
units.anchor: Always review and verify AI content and outputs

units.why: "AI tools can produce biased and inaccurate information" names bias as a risk, which is P53; the verification duty itself is coded in the previous unit as P31.
units.anchor: AI tools can produce biased and inaccurate information
units.fit_note: Type is about bias, harms and environmental cost; this mentions bias and inaccuracy only briefly.

units.why: "may include copyrighted information without attribution" flags copyright risk in AI output, so P52.
units.anchor: may include copyrighted information without attribution

units.why: "You are responsible for ensuring the accuracy and appropriateness of AI-generated content" puts accountability on the user for output they use, so P29 (own what is used and submitted).
units.anchor: You are responsible for ensuring the accuracy and appropriateness of AI-generated content

units.why: "you must follow the same security processes and risk assessments" for purchasing AI applications is a procurement-review rule, which is P65 (review AI vendor agreements).
units.anchor: you must follow the same security processes and risk assessments
units.policy: Anyone considering purchasing an AI application for use at Rutgers must follow the same security processes and risk assessments as for other software purchases, as well as standards for digital accessibility.
units.fit_note: Covers purchase review via security and accessibility standards, not data-sharing limits with providers.

units.why: The page lists the Acceptable Use Policy for IT Resources 70.1.1 as relevant to AI use, making AI subject to existing university policy (P77).
units.anchor: Outlines the acceptable use of university information technology resources

units.why: The page lists the Information Classification Policy 70.1.2 as relevant to AI, tying AI use to the existing data-protection policy (P77).
units.anchor: Outlines the standards for classifying information at Rutgers

notes: Only the Rutgers universitywide OIT guidance was coded; no Camden-specific or computing-unit documents were included in collect.
